content: 1. Lesions classified as ICC refer to invasive cervical cancer. The abbreviation nr indicates that data was not reported. 2. Standard deviation (SD), interquartile range (IQR), and range are statistical measures used to describe data variability. 3. For CIN2+ (Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia grade 2 or higher), the risk of bias was assessed using the Quality in Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool. 4. High bias (H) suggests that the relationship between the prognostic factor and outcome is very likely to differ between study participants and eligible non-participants. 5. Moderate bias (M) indicates that the relationship between the prognostic factor and outcome may differ between participants and eligible non-participants. 6. Low bias (L) implies that the relationship between the prognostic factor and outcome is unlikely to differ between participants and eligible non-participants. 7. Cytology data could not be allocated due to the study period not being reported in the manuscript. 8. LLETZ (Large Loop Excision of the Transformation Zone) and cryotherapy were used as treatment methods. 9. In 2013-2016, antiretroviral therapy (ART) was initiated when CD4 cell counts were ≤500 cells/mm³. From 2016 onwards, treatment was provided universally. 10. WLHIV refers to women living with human immunodeficiency virus. 11. LLETZ is a procedure involving the excision of the transformation zone, while cone biopsy refers to the removal of a cone-shaped section of abnormal tissue. 12. The QUIPS tool was used to assess the risk of bias in studies, categorizing it as high, moderate, or low based on the likelihood of differences in outcomes between participants and non-participants. 13. A systematic review was conducted to update the 2012 WHO guidelines for screening and treating precancerous cervical lesions, with additional terms included for HIV. 14. The search strategy prioritized sensitivity for systematic reviews and included databases such as Medline, Embase, Central, and LILACs, covering studies from 2012 to the present without language restrictions. 15. Studies from the previous WHO guidelines, including those involving women with HIV, were reviewed. 16. Individual patient data meta-analysis (IPD-MA) was conducted due to limited evidence and scarce age-specific data in the literature. 17. Authors of studies with at least 40 WLHIV and CIN2+ were contacted to contribute anonymized individual patient data for analysis. 18. Data from key studies, both published and unpublished, were pooled for analysis. 19. Examples of studies include cross-sectional and randomized controlled trials conducted in Kenya, Burkina Faso, Thailand, and the USA, involving HIV-positive women screened using cytology, HPV testing, and visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA). 20. A total of 12,527 HIV-positive participants and 49,365 HIV-negative participants were included across all datasets. 21. Data harmonization involved mapping variables to a master list provided by WHO, resolving discrepancies with investigators, and combining aligned datasets. 22. The IPD-MA used generalized linear mixed models to account for heterogeneity among studies, with diagnostics performed to ensure model fit. 23. Predicted probabilities for cervical screening results were calculated by age, HIV status, and other factors of interest. 24. Subgroup analysis focused on cases with confirmed histopathological diagnoses, examining probabilities of CIN2/3 diagnoses by age among WLHIV. 25. Histopathology diagnoses were categorized as negative/CIN1, CIN2/3, adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS), invasive cervical cancer (ICC), or other/indeterminate. 26. Among WLHIV, 6% of screening test results were confirmed by histopathology from biopsy. 27. The systematic review highlighted limited data on age-specific outcomes for WLHIV, necessitating the IPD-MA approach. 28. The WHO guideline development group decided against a comprehensive literature review for certain questions, opting instead for a Good Practice Statement based on available evidence. 29. Updated systematic reviews of treatments for CIN2, CIN3, and adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS) were conducted, focusing on ablative and excisional procedures. 30. The guideline group acknowledged challenges in differentiating CIN2 from CIN3 histologically and maintained current recommendations while noting the potential for future data, particularly for WLHIV. 31. Inclusion criteria for studies required histologically confirmed CIN2/3 or AIS/CIS lesions eligible for ablative or excisional treatment, with follow-up information available. 32. The search strategy included databases up to January 2020, identifying systematic reviews and primary studies on the progression and regression of untreated CIN2 under active surveillance. 33. Most studies included fewer than 100 women, with a median follow-up of 16 months (range: 3-72 months). 34. Non-compliance to treatment after diagnosis was reported in some studies, with durations between diagnosis and treatment typically less than six months. 35. The guideline group emphasized the importance of timely treatment for high-grade lesions and noted discrepancies in grading between biopsy-based and excision-based methods. 36. The updated systematic review included studies on cryotherapy, LEEP, and cold knife conization, with limited data on baseline CIN and post-treatment outcomes. 37. The group concluded that current recommendations should remain unchanged due to the difficulty in differentiating CIN2 from CIN3 histologically. 38. Future data, particularly for WLHIV, may provide additional insights into treatment outcomes and recommendations.
